Acceptance criteria checklist

Every acceptance criterion for this story, mapped to where it's demonstrated.

1

HR/Manager sees the directory on open — AC1

With "Signed in as" set to HR or Manager, the Directory screen loads straight into the full, searchable table of employee records.

2

Non-HR/Manager access is denied — AC2

Switch "Signed in as" to Employee or Signed out: the Directory and Profile screens both replace all content with an "Access denied" panel — search, filters, and the ID lookup are not rendered at all. See "Access & search reference".

3

Search/filter by name, department, or role returns only matches — AC3

Type a name, or choose a Department and/or Role, and the table narrows live to only the matching records — try combining all three.

4

No-match criteria show no results — AC4

Combine filters that no employee satisfies (e.g. Marketing + "Sales Manager") to see the empty state, with a "Clear filters" action.

5

Deactivated employees still appear, marked Inactive — AC5

Marcus Chen and Lena Voss are deactivated and still show up in the unfiltered directory and in name search, each with a distinct "Inactive" badge next to their name.

6

Status is not offered as a filter — AC6

The filter bar offers only Search, Department, and Role — there is no status dropdown, and the note beneath the filter bar calls this out explicitly.

7

A deactivated employee's record opens directly by ID — AC7

Enter emp_c003 (Marcus Chen) or emp_c008 (Lena Voss) into "Look up by employee ID" — the full record opens even though no filter was applied to find it.

8

An active employee's full record opens by ID or from the directory — AC8

Enter emp_c001 into the ID lookup, or click any active employee's name in the table — both open the same full record detail page.
